## Verified rule
In the demonstrated puzzle, a horizontal full-width line is the boundary/separator, and all other colored pieces are objects on one side of it. Importantly, when components collide they may stop against another piece, and distinct pieces can be stacked at different rows, not all moved to a uniform row. The corrected answer was accepted after changing only the placement of the color-4 vertical piece at (row 2, col 8): the first wrong output placed that cell at col 8 in row 1 (so the two-cell vertical 4 pair sat together at rows 2-3); correct output places the top 4 at row 2, col 8 and bottom at row 3, col 8 as given? Translate them toward the full-width boundary along the perpendicular axis, without changing their cross-axis positions. Simulate collision constraints: each shape moves until the next cell of it would overlap the boundary or an already settled object. For mutually interacting parts, resolve packing with a consistent order based on distance to the boundary; verify against the demo that each object is placed at the nearest available position. Do not make ad hoc assumptions that every piece simply shifts the same number of rows, or use arbitrary stacks based on eye estimation.
